Hub / company-study note · Maps to Course 04 (Competitive Strategy), Course 02 (Corporate Finance & Valuation), Course 11 (Global Strategy, Macro & Responsible Business), E2 (Capital Allocation), E3 (M&A), E7 (High-Stakes Communication), E8 (Stakeholder & Investor Relations), E10 (Digital & AI Transformation) · Written 2026-10-25 · Entry point for the ten BlackRock notes

  • Source: a filtered BlackRock corpus of 103 records, 2019-01 → 2026-10 (_ingest/raw/blackrock/index.tsv, full texts in articles.jsonl, about 1.7M characters). It covers:
  • 13 Fink letters, read in full;
  • 51 investor-relations releases, filtered from 164;
  • 25 newsroom items, filtered from 112;
  • 3 AGM transcripts (2021–23);
  • the 2023 and 2025 Investor Day decks, plus the GIP, Preqin and HPS deal decks;
  • the BUIDL launch release, the Fink–Goldstein Economist op-ed, and 4 cross-references from the Tradeweb corpus.

The filter and the gaps are documented in _ingest/raw/blackrock/DIGEST.md; the main gaps are no earnings-call transcripts and no AGM transcripts after 2023. Reader notes A–F are in _ingest/raw/blackrock/reading-notes/. - Core claim: BlackRock in 2019–2026 is three stories stacked on one engine. - The engine: record flows, from $124B to $698B a year, led by iShares, plus Aladdin. - Story 1, market structure. The largest buy-side client turns its software into the hub that venues, data vendors and custodians plug into. Then it multi-sources or internalizes around every concentrated supplier. - Story 2, strategy. In 2024–25 it spends ~$27B on GIP, Preqin and HPS to become "a scale operator across public and private markets and technology". This is a bet on a higher multiple. - Story 3, voice. Larry Fink's letters retreat in stages, from "a fundamental reshaping of finance" (2020) to "energy abundance" (2026), under a two-front political attack, while the fiduciary line (not our money) stays the constant. - What is never named: Tradeweb, despite being BlackRock's integrated credit venue. Also missing from the documents: a successor to Fink, and any metric for its own systemic weight.

3. Five patterns across the notes

  1. Multi-source the supplier, own the workflow. - Custodians (four), proxy advisers (Egan-Jones), exchanges (TXSE), dealers ("multiple intermediaries") and venues (internal crossing) are all treated the same way. - Aladdin is the workflow everyone plugs into. Venues court it. - This is the other side of tradeweb outside voices and tradeweb mission forces (buyer power), and of the coming venue consolidation (ice hub, marketaxess hub).
  2. Wrap the new thing in an old wrapper. - ETFs for bonds (2002 onward), ETPs for bitcoin (2024), money-market structures for tokenized cash (BUIDL) and SMAs or target-date funds for private markets (2025–26). - BlackRock monetizes innovations others built by packaging them for its distribution (blackrock digital assets, blackrock private markets).
  3. Buy the data layer, then the index. - The sequence runs from eFront (2019) to Clarity AI and Baringa (2021) to Preqin (2024). - The aim is to "index private markets just like we do now with the S&P 500" (Fink, 2025), moving BlackRock from index licensee to index owner (blackrock aladdin data). That puts it up against spglobal hub, lseg hub and bloomberg hub.
  4. The fiduciary hinge. Not our money is the argument for activism (2020), for neutrality (2023), against the right (DOJ/FTC) and against the left (Lander). The principle stays constant while the policy swings (blackrock fink letters, blackrock stewardship backlash).
  5. Self-measured scorecards. These are the BlackRock counterpart of the Tradeweb study's pattern 4 (tradeweb hub §3). All are BlackRock's own benchmarks: - execution savings ("25%" in 2023, "~$600 million" in 2024); - deal IRRs (15–18%); - the private-asset uplift in target-date funds (+50bp); - the "sustainability premium" (2021); - user counts whose definitions keep changing.

5. Cross-note open questions

  1. Succession: does a co-signatory, President or co-CEO appear by the 2027 letter? (blackrock people)
  2. Coal antitrust ruling: what does it mean for common ownership? (blackrock stewardship backlash)
  3. Private-markets scorecard: fundraising against ~$67B a year toward $400B; private markets plus technology against 30% of revenue. (blackrock private markets, blackrock strategy financials)
  4. Aladdin–venue terms after ICE–MarketAxess and Tradeweb–Trumid. (blackrock anchor client)
  5. Preqin indices: licensed to third parties? (blackrock aladdin data)
  6. BUIDL as collateral at venues or clearing houses. (blackrock digital assets)

Rep

Write a one-page memo as a Tradeweb board member: How dependent are we on BlackRock, and what do we do about it? Use only numbers from these notes and the Tradeweb notes.

  1. Size BlackRock's credit flow, using the blackrock anchor client Rep (≈277 AllTrade trades a day from Aladdin).
  2. Name BlackRock's three outside options: other venues, internalization, and Aladdin's integrations with rivals.
  3. Name Tradeweb's three counter-moves: Trumid, curated select smart RFQ, and co-investing in rails (Securitize).
  4. State the one number you would ask BlackRock for, and the one you would never get.

Then compare your memo with how Tradeweb's own releases describe the partnership (tradeweb credit §1).
